Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This revision application has been filed against the order dated 30.06.2022 passed by the learned Additional Principal Judge, Additional Family Court, Bermo at Tenughat (Bokaro) in Original Maintenance Case No. 325/2019, whereby the petitioner has been directed to pay Rs. 15,000/- per month to the opposite party No. 2 and Rs. 10,000/- to the opposite party No. 3 from the date of filing of the case i.e. 08.11.2019.
3.

sentences.text:
(a) An amount of Rs. 21,00,000/- was given to the opposite party No. 2 in terms of order dated 18.01.2020 passed in A.B.A. No. 9216 of 2019 whereby the petitioner has been granted anticipatory bail and in the said case, it was clearly recorded that the amount of Rs. 21,00,000/-
received by the informant (wife) be adjusted with respect to maintenance in any present or future proceeding between the parties or final settlement between the parties, if and when the same takes place.

The learned counsel has submitted that the amount of Rs. 21,00,000/- has been kept in Monthly Income Scheme (MIS) by the opposite party No. 2 and the learned court ought to have directed adjustment of the said amount and till the adjustment was complete, there was no occasion to grant any maintenance to the opposite party No. 2 and the minor daughter (opposite party No. 3).

(b) The learned counsel has also submitted that the opposite party No. 2 had suppressed material fact in her affidavit of disclosure of assets and liabilities, inasmuch as, she did not disclose that an amount of Rs. 8,000/- per month was being earned by her as interest on Rs. 21,00,000/-.

4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2 has submitted that the MIS was due to be renewed on 10.08.2024 and the opposite party No. 2 proposes to renew the MIS so that she would continue to get the interest on the same.

The learned counsel has submitted that if this Court is inclined to pass any order regarding adjustment of Rs. 21,00,000/-, the same can be adjusted only in connection with the maintenance granted to the wife.
So far as the daughter is concerned, there is no question of any adjustment.

5. He has also submitted that the maintenance was directed to be given with effect from November 2019 and as per up to date calculation by adjusting Rs. 15,000/- per month against the maintenance given to the wife, an amount of Rs. 8,70,000/- only can be said to have been adjusted.
6. The learned counsel further submits that so far as the suppression of fact in the affidavit of disclosures of assets and liabilities is concerned, the same is disputed.
He has also submitted that the income of Rs. 8,000/- per month from MIS had already been taken into consideration by the learned court.
7. Apart from the aforesaid arguments, no other argument has been advanced by the learned counsel for the parties.

8. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court finds that there is no dispute with regard to relationship between the petitioner and the opposite party No. 2.
It is also not in dispute that a minor daughter has been borne out of wedlock.

9. This Court finds that at the time of grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner in A.B.A. No. 9216 of 2019, this Court directed that the petitioner be given the privilege of anticipatory bail and it was also directed that in the event of his arrest or surrender within a period of four months from the date of the order, he shall be released on bail on depositing a demand draft of Rs. 21,00,000/- as ad Md. Imran vs State Of Jharkhand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27762950/
2 interim victim compensation in favour of informant (wife).

entities.text: ad Md. Imran vs State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also directed that in case, the said amount is received by the informant, the same shall be adjusted with respect to the maintenance in any present or future proceeding between the parties or final settlement between the parties, if and when the same takes place.

10. This Court is of the considered view that the daughter was not a party to the said proceedings of anticipatory bail as the case was arising out of alleged offence under Section 498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

11. In such circumstances, the argument of the petitioner that the amount of Rs. 21,00,000/- is to be adjusted also against the maintenance which has been granted to the minor daughter is misconceived and accordingly the same is hereby rejected.

12. So far as the allegation of the petitioner that the opposite party No. 2 had suppressed material facts before the concerned court, this Court is of the considered view that such plea was required to be taken before the learned court itself and there is no scope for raising such plea in the revisional jurisdiction.
This Court further finds that the fact that the informant was getting Rs. 8,000/- as interest on Rs. 21,00,000/- stood admitted as recorded in the impugned order.
Accordingly, the allegation made by the petitioner regarding suppression of material fact by the opposite party No. 2 (wife) is hereby rejected.

13. So far as the adjustment of Rs. 21,00,000/- against the maintenance which has been awarded to the wife is concerned, this Court is of the considered view that it is for the opposite party No. 2 (wife) to utilize amount of Rs. 21,00,000/- in any manner she wants to and it appears that she has chosen to invest that amount in a monthly income scheme.

However, in view of clear-cut observation made by this Court in A.B.A. No. 9216 of 2019, the amount of maintenance which has been given to the wife by the impugned order amounting to Rs. 15,000/- for herself is to be adjusted against Rs. 21,00,000/-.
It appears that if the period from November 2019 is taken into consideration, an amount of Rs. 8,70,000/- would stand adjusted.

14. This Court is of the view that unless the entire amount of Rs. 21,00,000/- stands adjusted with respect to the maintenance given to the wife, the wife will not be entitled for payment on account of maintenance as awarded by the impugned order.
Once the entire 21 Lakhs is covered, further payment would revive.

15. So far as the maintenance to the minor daughter is concerned, the petitioner shall continue to pay the same including arrears in terms of the impugned order and such award of maintenance does not call for any interference.
16. This petition is disposed of in the aforesaid terms .
17. Pending I.A., if any, is closed.

18. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the court concerned through 'e-mail/FAX'.
